issues.legal_issue: An arbitration award that directs the parties to execute later documents to create or transfer rights in immovable property is not compulsorily registrable when the award itself does not create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish those rights.
material_facts: The parties referred their disputes to a sole arbitrator, whose award concerned immovable property valued above the statutory threshold for compulsory registration.
The award directed the property-holding company to execute documents declaring the other parties’ shares and transferring the property and lease into joint names.
The High Court held that the award required registration and could not be made a rule of court because it was unregistered.
The Supreme Court concluded that the award itself did not create or alter rights in the property; it created a right to obtain later documents that would do so.
issues.conclusion: The award fell within section 17(2)(v) of the Registration Act and was not compulsorily registrable. The High Court’s ruling was reversed and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act, a document is compulsorily registrable if it itself purports or operates to create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish the specified rights in immovable property. Under section 17(2)(v), a document that merely creates a right to obtain another document that will create or alter those rights is not compulsorily registrable. The Court applied Rajangam Ayyar v. Rajangam Ayyar, Sheonarain Lal v. Rameshwari Devi, Satish Kumar v. Surinder Kumar, and Ratan Lal Sharma v. Purshottam Harit to distinguish an award that itself effects rights in property from one that requires a later instrument to do so.

predicates.appeal_from_registration_based_rejection: An appeal challenges a decision rejecting an arbitration award from admission or enforcement because it was not registered.
predicates.arbitration_award_orders_future_property: An arbitrator directs a party to execute later documents to declare or transfer rights in immovable property.
predicates.award_does_not_itself_alter_property_rig: The award itself does not create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish rights in the property, but only gives a right to obtain a later document that will do so.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a registration-based rejection of an arbitration award that requires later property documents but does not itself alter property rights, the award is not compulsorily registrable.
